squirrel-removal.intro: Latta is a Dillon County town on the I-95 corridor in the flat Pee Dee — a small, tree-lined community of older homes standing in farm country between the Little Pee Dee's swamps and the fields. Its squirrels are swamp-edge squirrels: gray squirrels in numbers, working the town's big oaks and the pecan trees in the older yards, denning in the attics of the pre-war homes through the winter and raising litters in them in the warm months. The flat country puts the canopy at roof height across most of Latta, so the classic entry — the chewed soffit corner under an overhanging limb — is available on nearly every street, and the colonies use it.
squirrel-removal.extendedBody:
Flat country, low roofs, easy bridges

Latta's squirrel work is bridge work. Where the canopy stands at roof height and the houses are one and two stories, squirrels reach the roofline from the trees, the fences, and the power lines without ever crossing open ground — so the inspection reads the approaches as carefully as the entries: which limbs touch, which lines land on the roof, where the fence meets the eave. The colony is excluded with one-way devices, the chewed entries rebuilt in metal, and the bridges mapped for trimming with the specific limbs named. Inside, the attic tells the tenancy's length — leaf-nest material, nut caches, droppings — and the wiring is checked where the colony has been established. Pee Dee farm country also stocks Latta with a second squirrel fact: the surrounding woods hold more squirrels than the town ever will, so the seal is the whole job. A trapped-out attic on an open roofline in Latta is re-let by the next dispersal, every time.

faqs.q: How much does squirrel removal cost in Latta?
faqs.a: It depends on the entries and the bridges — a single chewed corner with one limb to cut is a compact job; a roofline reachable from three trees is a bigger read. We inspect the roof and its approaches, quote the exclusion, sealing, and bridge map firmly before work starts, and include the attic condition in the same report. The sealing is in metal, because in country with this many squirrels a patched-in-kind entry is a door left ajar.

faqs.q: Why do squirrels keep coming back to our Latta street every year?
faqs.a: Because the street offers the full package in a small area: canopy at roof height, pecan and oak mast through the fall, and attics with entries that were patched rather than sealed. Squirrels are not wandering randomly — they hold territories and revisit proven dens, and their young disperse each fall to the nearest available roofs. The houses that break the pattern are the sealed ones: metal at the entries, bridges cut. A street does not need every house sealed to quiet down; it needs the den houses closed, and yours can be one of them this season.
